data.name: a2a
data.label: 🔌 A2A
data.description:
A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol v1.0 support for Hermes Agent — both directions of the open Linux Foundation standard for inter-agent communication.
OUTBOUND (client tools): a2a_discover, a2a_call, a2a_list, a2a_history, and a2a_orchestrate let the agent fetch another agent's Agent Card and send it tasks over JSON-RPC — works with any A2A-compliant peer (Hermes, LangChain, CrewAI, Google ADK, OpenClaw, ...).
INBOUND (platform adapter): exposes Hermes as an A2A-discoverable agent. An Agent Card is served at /.well-known/agent-card.json (v1.0 canonical path; legacy agent.json also answers) and incoming tasks are routed into the agent's live gateway session like any other platform — so the agent that replies is the same one talking to its user, with full memory and context, not a throwaway clone.
Security is on by default: no bearer token configured => localhost-only bind. Inbound task text passes through prompt-injection filters; outbound text is scrubbed of credential-shaped strings; every exchange is audit-logged and persisted to disk outside the context-compaction pipeline so conversations survive compaction and restarts.
Pure stdlib transport (http.server + urllib) — no a2a-sdk dependency required.

data.name: availability
data.label: 🔌 Availability
data.description: Turn a spoken field walk into an unpriced, customer-facing availability list: resolve each item against the operator's own catalogue, normalise the quantity and unit, and keep what could not be matched rather than dropping it. The list carries no prices by design.

data.name: claims
data.label: 🔌 Claims
data.description: Lint marketing copy for claims: health claims refused outright, certification and environmental claims named with the record that would have to stand behind them, and provenance and comparative claims flagged for substantiation. It reports; it never rewrites.

data.name: connectors
data.label: 🔌 Connectors
data.description: Use the apps the operator has connected through Composio. The service holds the key and the connection; this plugin lets the assistant read through it and escalates every write to the engine's human-approval gate before anything leaves the machine.

data.name: consent
data.label: 🔌 Consent
data.description: The pre-send gate for direct marketing: one decision per recipient from the consent records — allowed, no record, withdrawn, or ambiguous — plus the two draft checks, sender identification and an unsubscribe line. It refuses a send with no consent record.

data.name: invoicing
data.label: 🔌 Invoicing
data.description: pantler's own tools: draft an invoice from the operator's price book and read a saved draft back from the record store. Nothing here is sent — the draft is written into the money pack so it survives a restart, and the number is reserved in the store so it is never issued twice. The plugin also registers the profile-scope guard that keeps another business's workspace and profile state out of this one.

data.name: records
data.label: 🔌 Records
data.description: Read and write the operator's own records — certificates, spray applications, blocks, harvests — through the kernel's record store, validated against the pack that declares them. The model extracts what the operator said; this tool decides whether it is a record.

data.name: soil
data.label: 🔌 Soil
data.description: Read an EAL soil certificate of analysis and return a structured soil amendment program - base saturations, element deficits, product rates with annual caps, and named rule codes. The tool returns data; the model writes the narrative.

data.name: spray
data.label: 🔌 Spray
data.description: Record an application against the operator's own spray book: resolve the block and the product, multiply the rate by the area, and date the earliest safe harvest from the withholding period on file. The tool returns the record; the model writes the narrative.
